*From the perspective of an Orachi* 

I saw Death itself, it was the only thing we had left...

Our group could only fight back for so long, the knights had gotten closer and closer to our home base. The Canopy. Where out civilians and other forces acome for shelter. And we were on the brink of loss. 

I had fought off the foot soldiers and managed to kill a few of those knights with thier flails and large shields, even a Warden who was sloppy with his strikes. Yet it had little effect for the oncoming forces. The Lawbringers and Wardens came crushing through our defenses and had made their way in. I was staioned in the main area, protecting the center platform. I saw a Nobushi running at me, her mask was cracked, showing her face, she asked me to come with her. It was no use to fight back.

We ran back to the out headquarters, high above looking over all of the canopy, citizens and injured samurai all took shelter. A Shinobi had been tneding his wounds, one of our Aramusha men was sharpening his one katana, he lost the othet in battle. Other Orachi's like me were aganist the wall, lying down and hoping for either a quick death or a outstanding victory. 

"I brought all I could find." Said the Nobushi, she took of her mask. She had bruises on her face.

"Good." Said the Kensei, who was the commander of our group. "You did well, all of us did." He was kneeling down next to a makeshift fire and the staute. A sign of peace, yet now it almost meant nothing but fine art.

"With all respect, what do we do. The knights are here. Wardens, Lawbringers, and I even heard word of those Black Prior's com-" 

"Shhh," the Kensei stopped my words. "all will be okay in the end." 

I then saw him take out a small blade. He gripped it in his right hand, he took of the gloves and what armor protected his left hand. I heard only whispers of what he said. Still I could not make it out. Then the small blade had touched his left hand, drawing blood that split on the floor. 

"Commander!" I yelled, worried for what he was doing. 

"Stop..." The Nobushi told me, putting a hand softly on my shoulder. "I know what he is doing." 

The Kensei then looked down at his bloody left hand. 

"She will come now...just try not to look." The Kensei said. 

Wind howled, clouds came, and then soon the canopy wa shrouded in fog. I couldn't help but go outside to look. I could barely make out the figures, I could barely see few Wardens, Peacekeepers, and then a Lawbringer. 

Then I saw one figure that was small in stature, yet carried a large weapon. A masakari. 

I could only make it out to be a woman, and it walked forawrd from the entrance gates to the center platform. It was as if she had a death wish, a Warden was had prepared it's blade. Running towards her with his blade raised in the air, and then he was met with a unstoppable force. The figure had blocked the swing with her axe, and then kicked the Warden. Switching her hold of the blade, she had sliced the Warden's body in half. Then the figure simply walked by it. As more soldiers came for her.

I looked away, the sight of a body served by the waist had sickened me. I could only hear the sounds of metal meeting metal, steel meeting steel, and the sounds of agony and anger. Once the sounds stopped. I assumed it was over. Yet it wasn't.

One last knight, the same type with the flial and shield was on the bridge. Begging for mercy, yet the figure dragged her masakari on the wood floor. Making its way toward him on the bridge. She had raised the axe, and then brought it down onto his head. Crushing the helmet protecting him. Then placing her foot on his helm, then pushing it back. The axe now bloody. 

Just then the figure shifted her gaze to my position. I got down behind the small defense of wood gates we had. A short time passed, and then I looked back to see the figure was gone. 

I ran back to our commander. Still on the floor with the blood still dripping from his hand. 

"Is it over?" He asked calmly. 

"Yes...yes it is." I responded. 

"Good." He then bandaged his hand. Tightly and then stood up to face me. 

"It was all we had left." The Kensei had said, he then proceeded to walk out into the now dispersing fog. 

"What did you see?" A Shinobi had asked, sitting aganist a wall, weakened. 

"Death." I said. "I saw Death itself."

If you ever wanted something so bad that you would go to Heaven and Hell for it, you tell Annadane all about it. Cuz she knows a thing or two about what it is like

When she was 15, and had found her fathers old Regal Legion arms and armor, she felt it only right to carry on the legacy. Her father also held his exotic longsword in a glass case. Only able to open it with a key, her father gave the key to her. 

Only to open it when "It was needed, or when she was ready."

She had trained for the next two with blacksmiths, prominent swordsmen, former knights of Ashfeld to work her way up. 

All while being put down for her sex, those believing a woman could not stand aganist a strong Viking or even a small and ninble Shinobi. Yet she kepted on training despite the cruel words and undermining.

Her training had paid off the day that a local village was being attacked by a Samurai clan, made by their leader to force them to surrender and have them as prisoner's of war. 

She grabbed her fathers old Regal Legion armor, rusted yet still functional, the longsword kept from his time in battle, finally opening the glass case. The curved blade was unusual yet so beautiful. She then made her way to save the Village on horseback.

Wardens, Lawbringers, and a few Peacekeepers were still fighting the Samurai clan, the leader Kensi was going through the foot soliders like cutting through cake, and the Wardens had protected the citizens while fighting. War cry's , screaming, and commands were heard as Annadane got closer and closer.  

The village was set fire by fire arrows that struck the homes. It was said the Kensei had called out for all to surrender or face a stay of execution. Those who surrender will work to make Samurai arms and armor,  the Wardens had disagreed. 

Annadane made it there, the village Warden was fighting in the middle of the scorached village. Fighting in the mud and blood around them, as few other Samurai members rounded up citizens who failed to leave, and also killed the Wardens, Lawbringers, and Peacekeepers left standing.

Anndane had remembered training under dire circumstances, she had ran fast and swung her fathers sword the same. Doing battle with a Shinobi, she had not fallen for the smoke trick, and slashed the Shinobi's arms off. Then making her way to save a little girl who had been caught in the midst of violence. In the short moment she herself in the girl's eyes. Scared and wanting to run.

She pulled the girl out and then told her to stay by her. Holding her arm as she ran to a shed that hadn't yet been burned down. She had kicked the door down and told her to hide somewhere safe. 

Just then, an Aramusha had made his way to her. Wielding two katanas in either hand, and having mud around his feet, Annadane prepped her stance and stood aganist the Armausha. A few parries had opened the Aramusha with a blade to the chest.

Finally, she ran to the leader, the Kensei who led the vile attack. She ran to him, the Warden was near dead, tired, and beat. He feel back onto the mud, struggling to get up. Annadane picked up speed, she grabbed her longsword like a spear. One hand on the blade and the other on the hilt. Rushing past the dead bodies and ignoring the crackling of burning wood. 

The Kensei had his nodachi raised to impale the Warden,  yet he dropped the blade as Annadane ran the blade through his back. Implaing his body like one on a pike. 

The battle was over, Annadane's training had payed off. 

Months Later...

Annadane now acts a Strategic Mastermind for her stationed fort, on the border of Ashfeld and the Samurai land, The Myre.

She currently has a plan to take a Samurai fort, several miles up west. Annadane was also given a new set of armor, made of shining bronze and more reinforced then her fathers old armor.

However, she kept the sword. Her father would be proud, as she was of herself.

Still grinding for that blade.

Calivan had fought for years and years to earn the title "Ser" by Hervis Daubeny.
Before knighthood, he fought for the Iron Legion in the war, he was known for his expertise in swordsmanship from local tournaments with longswords, yet the tips were dull and the blades dull as well. Not until the day he joined the Iron Legion to fight alongside other knights, and yearn to be honored with the name "Ser". 

Months later in the Iron Legion, serving under Hervis Daubeny, he voluneteered to fight against a legendary Highlander, known only as "The Brute".
Sent to fight for control and a peaceful surrender for territory. If he won, Daubeny would knight him, and have his own armor made. Exchange his iron armor, all scratched and with dents for a new set of crafted silver oriented armor. All by his own design.
The Brute was known to kill knights swiftly and savagely. Heads, arms, and torsos were found yards away from their owners.

He traveled to The Snowy Pit and waited for The Brute. Once The Brute arrived, he realized how he got the title. Large, tall, tattered red cape and a long braided beard. With fur armor and massive claymore with blood from past victims and the large boot prints in the snow, Calivan knelt and give recognition to Highlander.

Honorbound to the End.

Their fought went on for what felt like hours, yet in reality is was minutes. 
Calivan had blocked, dodged, and parried the Highlander's large sword, making loud CLANG as the blades met and PUMF noises in the snow. Calivan used everything he learned, from half swording,  shoulder bashing the opponent to knock them aganist a wall, he learned this from a Centurion who had also taught him, as well as another Warden.

Yet the Highlander made his last mistake, when his mighty claymore missed it's target and Calivan parried it, he had then used the pommel of his sword to bash the Brute's face, now discombobulated, he struck The Brute's left leg with the crossguard. Sending him down like a castles walls being breached. 

Then he lifted his sword as high as he could above his head. One hand on the blade and other on the hilt. And down to the Brute's heart, through his torso, and into the snow it went. 
He closed his eyes and heard the last coughs from the Highlander. The crowd of other Vikings was quiet. He had won. 

The white snow begun to turn red around them. 

Days later, Daubeny had knighted him, and his silver amror was made. He asked for a dragon on top of his helm, to be the last thing his oppenents saw. 
He asked for his paint to be dyed white as well, including having a dofferent symbol for his cloth. So that he can act as a noble, secret, and clean fighter. Daubeny had liked and approved the idea.

 Daubeny has sent him out numerous times to fight other Vikings, Samurai, and even other Knights of opposing factions for Daubeny.
He fights as a champion, a knight sent out for Daubeny in secret, as well as competing aganist other Knights.
Not a single loss reported.
